text:
maya: Ran a suite of canary perf experiments focused on perceived latency (token streaming chunk size + flush interval) and microbatch sizing. Comparing kernel variants + KV cache behavior too. Wanted to surface results and get opinions on default SLO tradeoffs.

henry: awesome — did you test with realistic seq distributions (mixed 64/256/1024)?

maya: yes, 70% short (<=128), 25% mid (256-512), 5% long (>1024). All runs used our prod-like arrival traces.

aj: curious numbers — p50/p95/p99 and throughput?

maya: pasted the condensed table below (each row is same model + weights, only microbatch/flush/chunk/kernel differ). KV hit is measured for prefix caching.

maya: ```
config | microbatch | flush_ms | chunk_tok | kv_hit | tp_tok/s | p50_ms | p95_ms | p99_ms
A      | 1          | 20       | 8         | 0.92   | 1800     | 30     | 120    | 340
B      | 4          | 40       | 16        | 0.97   | 1650     | 35     | 95     | 210
C      | 8          | 100      | 32        | 0.86   | 2000     | 28     | 150    | 520
D      | 4          | 25       | 8         | 0.95   | 1600     | 33     | 88     | 190
E      | 2          | adaptive | 12        | 0.96   | 1700     | 32     | 90     | 205
```

maya: Observations: B/D/E hit a much better p99 vs A/C. C has highest throughput but terrible tail (p99=520ms) due to occasional KV cache misses + long microbatch flush causing bursty schedule. A (microbatch=1, flush 20ms) gives low p50 but p99 still high because many tiny batches increase kernel dispatch overhead and cause straggling on lower-utilized GPUs.

henry: interesting that 4+25ms (D) gets almost same p95/p99 as 4+40ms (B) but slightly lower throughput. Means lowering flush_ms helps perceived latency without large throughput hit.

maya: yeah — flush_ms tuning gave diminishing returns after ~25-40ms for our mix. Also kernel selection matters: when we force the high-throughput fused kernel the p99 for mid-long sequences balloons (kernel stalls on KV lookups), while the generic kernel is slower avg but more stable.

aj: do we have perf traces showing where the tail comes from (kernel stall vs queuing vs network)?

maya: prof dump attached (summary inline):
maya: - tail samples show 60% time in "kv_lookup_wait" on long sequences, 25% in "kernel_kernel_launch_wait" (small batches), rest in memcpy.

maya: stack: ``kv_lookup_wait -> spawn_io -> kernel_launch`` — suggests KV cache serialization when many small chunks touch different cache shards.

perf-bot: NOTICE: canary run 1768894200 flagged p99 > 3x baseline for config C, regression ticket #INF-2489 opened.

sarah: given this, my vote is default config = B (microbatch=4, flush=40ms, chunk=16) for hosted API. It balances p99 and throughput and keeps KV hit high. For Dedicated customers we can expose knobs.

henry: agree but think we should add an adaptive flush that shrinks flush_ms when queue depth is low and increases slightly under sustained high q to preserve throughput. Our simulation of adaptive (E) matched B in tail but with smoother throughput.

aj: tradeoff quantification request: how much throughput do we sacrifice switching to B from C? numbers above show ~17.5% drop (2000->1650 tok/s). If a customer needs strict p99 we should let them pay for dedicated pools.

maya: also important: chunk_tok interacts with KV fragmentation. Larger chunk_tok (32) reduces number of KV lookups but increases first-token latency per chunk because we hold tokens until flush. So perceived streaming latency worsens even if overall throughput is higher.

sarah: ops question — any evidence changing kernel fallback policy (prefer generic for sequences >512) would reduce tail without huge cost?

maya: quick sim: routing >512 to generic drops p99 for those sequences by ~40% but overall throughput drop is <5% on our canary due to small percent long requests. So yes, recommend kernel routing by seq_len.

henry: action items?

maya: proposed: 
1) Default config for hosted: microbatch=4, flush_ms=35 (we'll try 35), chunk_tok=16.
2) Implement adaptive flush prototype in runtime (thresholds: q_len<=8 -> flush 20ms, q_len 9-32 -> 35ms, >32 -> 60ms).
3) Kernel routing: generic for seq_len>512, fused for <=512.
4) Improve KV shard mutex to reduce kv_lookup_wait serialization (low-priority infra task).
5) Add canary that measures perceived-first-token latency (cold vs warmed KV).

aj: +1. Can we make adaptive flush config per-customer? For Dedicated yes, Hosted maybe tiered.

maya: yes — we'll expose flags in rollout. I'll open a PR for adaptive flush and a canary run next week.

ops-bot: SCHEDULED: canary rollout window suggested Tue 09:00-11:00 PT to capture peak traffic.

sarah: thanks maya. If perf team agrees, let's merge kernel routing and adaptive flush to canary flags, monitor p50/p95/p99 + perc-first-token.

henry: one more note — add a metric for "stream-chunk-delay" (time between token generation and flush send) so app teams can correlate perceived latency to chunking.

maya: noted — will add metric and open INF-2498 for dashboard.

aj: thanks all. TL;DR: prefer moderate microbatch (4), moderate flush (~25-40ms), chunk ~16 for best p99 vs throughput tradeoff; add adaptive flush + seq_len kernel routing + KV contention fixes.
